title: service-call-graphs-and-cascading-failure-mitigation-playbook-2026
author: Aisha Kumar
content:
Title: Service Call Graphs and Cascading Failure Mitigation — Platform Playbook

Summary:
This playbook documents how Redwood’s platform teams should model service call graphs, detect emerging cascading failures, and apply mitigation patterns (circuit breakers, bulkheads, adaptive throttling) across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. It combines design guidelines, concrete dashboard and alert recommendations, incident runbooks, retrospective checklists, and a short roadmap for incremental improvements.

Scope:
- Applies to platform-facing services in the eng-platform and eng-serving-runtime domains (routing, model-proxy, cache-service, quota-service, autoscaler, sidecars).
- Not intended for application-level business logic (product teams should have their own fallbacks per SLAs).

Goals:
1. Reduce blast radius of failures that originate from downstream services by 80% for common dependency classes within 6 months.
2. Detect cascading patterns earlier using call-graph-derived composite SLOs and anomaly detection.
3. Provide a repeatable incident response runbook to restore service with minimal human coordination.

Definitions and Concepts:
- Call graph: Directed graph where nodes are services and edges are RPC/HTTP/call relationships with associated P95/P99 latency and error rate meta.
- Cascading failure: When degradation in a downstream node increases load or errors upstream, triggering a chain reaction.
- Circuit breaker: Logical switch to fail-fast or route around a failing dependency.
- Bulkhead: Resource partitioning technique (threadpools/connection pools/GPU pools) to limit cross-service interference.

Ownership:
- Platform Core (team lead: Miguel Torres) owns the canonical call-graph generation pipeline and visualization components.
- Observability (team lead: Priya Reddy) owns the alerting library and composite SLO definitions.
- Runtime (team lead: Sam Bennett) owns sidecar-level resilience primitives and rollout controls.

Observability (what to collect):
- Per-edge metrics: request_rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, error_rate (4xx/5xx split), retry_rate, queue_depth.
- Per-node metrics: concurrent_requests, cpu_util, mem_rss, thread_pool_busy_pct, inbound_rate, outbound_rate.
- Traces: sampled distributed traces with service and edge annotations (call_site, retry_type, circuit_state).
- Composite indicators: normalized downstream_health_score (0-1), cascading_index (0-100) derived by call-graph propagation.

Suggested dashboard panels (standardized across regions):
- "Service Heatmap": grid of downstream_health_score for top 50 dependencies.
- "Call Graph Live Topology": interactive view with edge thickness = request_rate and color = cascading_index.
- "Upstream Impact Table": top upstream services sorted by delta(error_rate) attributable to a single downstream failure.
- "Retry Storm Detector": retry_rate spike charts + source of retries (client vs internal).

Example dashboard layout (panel rows):
1) Overview: availability, composite SLOs, top anomalous edges
2) Topology: interactive call graph + node detail selector
3) Latency & Errors: P95/P99 by edge, error types, recent changes
4) Resource Pressure: queue_depth, thread pool saturation, connection pool exhaustion
5) Incident Signals: unusual fan-in/out, synchronized latency spikes across edges

Alerting: rules and thresholds
- Important: Avoid identical thresholds across different services — use risk tiers (Tier 0 critical infra, Tier 1 high-volume platform services, Tier 2 low-volume utilities).
- Basic edge alerts (Tier 1 example):
  * edge_error_rate > 4% for 3m (alert: paging)
  * p99_latency_increase >= 2x baseline for 2m AND request_rate_drop > 20% (alert: paging)
  * retry_rate_spike > 5x baseline for 1m (alert: on-call)
- Composite alerts (derived):
  * cascading_index > 30 for 5m => escalate to platform SRE lead
  * cross-service error correlation (>=3 upstreams show error_rate delta > 2%) => trigger incident bridge
- Alert routing: paging should go to the owning service on-call first. If cascading_index > 50 or multiple teams implicated, escalate to platform triage channel and platform core on-call.

SLO mapping and composite SLOs:
- Maintain per-service request_success SLO (e.g., 99.9% success over 30d) and downstream_dependency_availability SLO (95% for best-effort dependencies).
- Define composite SLOs that represent user-facing flows (e.g., "Model inference end-to-end"), computable by expanding call graphs and weighting edge SLOs by traffic contribution.
- Use composite SLO degradations as a primary signal to trigger rollback of recent platform changes or to activate graceful degradation.

Design Patterns and Libraries (how-to):
1. Circuit Breaker (recommended primitives):
   - Failure threshold: sliding window 60s, if error_rate > 5% and p99 > 2x baseline then open.
   - Half-open policy: allow 5% of requests through for 30s probe.
   - Fallback strategy: cached response or 503 with user-facing retry-after header where safe.
2. Bulkhead: partition pool by upstream caller type (control plane vs data plane). Default pool sizes defined per instance class in config table below.
3. Adaptive Backpressure: when downstream queue_depth > 75% of configured max, start shedding or downgrade non-essential requests (e.g., telemetry writes).
4. Retry policy: exponential backoff with jitter; max attempts: 3 for idempotent calls, 0 for non-idempotent. Do not retry on 4xx errors except 429.

Config table (defaults — tune per service):
| config_key | default_value | notes |
|-----------|---------------|-------|
| thread_pool_size | 128 | medium instance; reduce for small utility services |
| connection_pool_max | 64 | per-upstream pool |
| queue_max_items | 10000 | used by adaptive backpressure |
| circuit_failure_threshold_pct | 5 | percent errors in sliding window to open |
| circuit_window_seconds | 60 | size of sliding window |
| bulkhead_partitions | 3 | reservations for control/data/unknown traffic |

Incident Runbook: Cascading Failure (quick restore)
1. Triage (0-5 min):
   a. Open incident bridge and post incident header with initial hypothesis.
   b. Identify the high cascading_index node(s) via the topology panel.
   c. If cascading_index < 20, monitor and rate-limit alerts; if >=20, proceed to mitigation.
2. Containment (5-15 min):
   a. For each implicated downstream node, toggle circuit breaker to "open" (fail fast) for non-essential call paths using rollout flag.
   b. Apply temporary routing rule to route critical traffic to a known-good region or model variant if available.
   c. Reduce global client concurrency for affected upstreams via per-route quotas (throttle by 30%).
3. Mitigation (15-60 min):
   a. If a specific service shows resource exhaustion, increase pool limits or restart worker pool if safe (use canary restart first).
   b. If error cause is degeneration (e.g., bad cache corruption), perform targeted cache invalidation.
   c. If root cause unknown, enable extended tracing for affected edges (increase sampling to 100% for 10 minutes).
4. Recovery (60-180 min):
   a. Gradually close circuit breakers and ramp concurrency with canary checks and health probes.
   b. Monitor composite SLO and cascading_index for regression.
   c. Once stable for 2x SLO window, close incident and begin retrospective.

Runbook commands and quick snippets:
- Toggle circuit via admin CLI: redwood-circuitctl set --service model-proxy --dependency quota-service --state open --reason "cascade-mitigation"
- Increase thread pool (safe restart): kubectl -n platform scale deployment model-proxy --replicas=3 && apply configmap threadpool=192
- Increase tracing sampling (temporarily): curl -X POST http://obs-controlplane/api/sampling -d '{"service":"model-proxy","rate":1.0}'

Postmortem & Retrospective Checklist:
- Capture timeline with signal timestamps (alerts, mitigations applied, service changes).
- Identify earliest signal: was this an edge anomaly, resource exhaustion, configuration change, or external dependency?
- Quantify blast radius: affected services, customer impact, error budget burn.
- Action items: assign owners, set due dates, and prioritize in platform roadmap. Typical action examples:
  * Add top-10 dependency heatmap to weekly on-call dashboard (owner: Observability).
  * Harden circuit-breaker tuning for the quota-service (owner: Runtime).
  * Add regression test for the failing call pattern in CI (owner: Eng-Devex).
- Retro: schedule 60-min cross-team review with platform, runtime, and observability within 3 business days.

Testing & Pre-deployment Validation:
- Chaos test: simulate downstream latency and saturated queues for 30s and validate that the upstream service’s retries, circuit-breakers, and bulkheads behave within thresholds.
- Synthetic flows: run black-box synthetic composite SLO checks (end-to-end) against canary cluster prior to major rollout.
- Load tests: include fan-in scenarios that replicate typical production call graph degrees (e.g., 1:50).

Roadmap (next 6 months):
- Q2 2026: Canonical call-graph ingest pipeline (owner: Platform Core) — export per-deployment graphs to the topology service and persist weekly snapshots.
- Q3 2026: Composite SLO engine GA (owner: Observability) — define user flows and automated rollback triggers.
- Q4 2026: Automated circuit tuning (owner: Runtime) — leverage reinforcement signals to recommend/roll optimal circuit thresholds.
- Ongoing: Add regional policies for private deployments (on-prem) to respect customer network constraints.

Operational Playbook Notes (team wiki items):
- Nightly job: snapshot call graph and run heuristics to precompute top-25 dangerous dependency pairs; email to platform lead.
- Weekly runbook drill: 30-min tabletop on cascading scenario with at least one cross-team participant.
- Documentation: keep service-level fallback contracts published in each service repo README and link from the call-graph node metadata.

Appendix A: Incident examples (anonymized)
- Case 1: Quota-service connection pool leak (Jan 2026) — symptoms: upstream p99 climb and synchronized retries. Mitigation: opened circuit breakers, drained stale connections, rollout of connection pool fix.
- Case 2: Cache corruption (Nov 2025) — symptoms: mass 500s with low downstream cpu but high queue_depth. Mitigation: cache invalidation + gradual restart.
